decision.title: Launch Product X in Q2 2025 vs Wait for Q3
decision.description: We need to decide whether to launch our new SaaS product in Q2 2025 as planned, or delay until Q3 to add advanced features and improve quality. The market window is closing as competitors are also launching similar products.
decision.context: Product X is a project management tool targeting mid-market companies. Current development is 85% complete. We have $200K remaining budget for marketing. Three competitors are launching similar products in Q3. Our beta users (500+) report 4.2/5 satisfaction.
goals: Achieve 10K paid users within 6 months of launch
Generate $500K ARR by end of year
constraints: Can't hire additional staff until post-launch
decision.timeframe: Decision needed by March 15, 2025. Q2 launch = April 1. Q3 launch = July 1.

scenarios.title: Critical bugs cause mass user churn
scenarios.description: Launch with remaining bugs leads to poor user experience. App crashes frequently, data sync fails, and users abandon the platform within first week. Negative reviews tank app store rating to 2.5/5.

scenarios.title: Competitor launches first and captures market
scenarios.description: By waiting until Q3, competitors launch in Q2 with similar features and better marketing. They capture early adopters and establish brand recognition. We enter a crowded market as a follower, not a leader.

scenarios.title: Marketing budget insufficient for Q2 launch
scenarios.description: Rushing to market in Q2 means less time for marketing preparation. $200K budget gets spread too thin across multiple channels. Launch generates weak initial traction (only 1K users in first month instead of target 5K).

scenarios.title: Team burnout from rushing launch
scenarios.description: Pushing for Q2 launch requires 60-hour work weeks for 8 weeks. Engineers burn out, make mistakes, and two key developers quit immediately after launch. This cripples post-launch support and feature development.

scenarios.title: Advanced features delay causes Q3 miss too
scenarios.description: If we delay to Q3 for advanced features, scope creep pushes launch to Q4. Competitors dominate market by then. We miss fiscal year targets and investor confidence drops.

rootCauses.description: Insufficient QA testing time (only 2 weeks allocated)
Complex data sync architecture prone to edge cases
Competitors have larger marketing budgets and earlier start
Unrealistic timeline without considering team capacity
Advanced features not well-defined (scope creep risk)

mitigations.strategy: Extend QA phase by 4 weeks, hire contract QA specialist for critical path testing
Simplify data sync for v1.0, move advanced sync to v1.1 post-launch
Focus on niche differentiation (better integrations) rather than competing on features
Hire freelance marketing consultant, start pre-launch campaign 6 weeks before launch
Add 2-week buffer to timeline, implement mandatory weekend rest policy
Lock advanced features list today, commit to v1.1 roadmap instead of v1.0 scope creep

factors: High-impact bugs highly likely with current timeline
Scope creep risk if delaying to Q3

evidence.title: Beta user feedback: crash rate concerns
evidence.content: Beta testing shows crash rate of 8% on iOS devices, particularly on iPhone 14 Pro. Users report data sync failures when switching between devices. Sample size: 500 beta users over 4 weeks.

evidence.title: Competitor launch timeline (public info)
evidence.content: Competitor A announced Q2 launch at their conference. Competitor B leaked Q3 date in press release. Competitor C (stealth mode) rumored for Q2 based on hiring patterns and domain registrations.

evidence.title: Historical data: rushed launches fail
evidence.content: Analysis of 50 SaaS launches from 2020-2024 shows rushed launches (< 3 months QA) have 65% higher churn in first 90 days. Products that delayed for quality improvements saw 40% higher retention.

evidence.title: CTO opinion: need 6 more weeks
evidence.content: CTO assessment: 'Current code quality is not production-ready. We need minimum 6 additional weeks for refactoring critical paths and comprehensive testing. Rushing will cause technical debt that takes 6 months to fix.'

conversationHistory.content: I need to decide whether to launch Product X in Q2 2025 or wait until Q3. What should I consider?
